errors.name: Check
errors.comment: Check can be used for negative validations on an object.

param.name: F
param.comment: F is the name of the object causing the failed check, for example, a filename

param.name: Err
param.comment: Err is the error causing the failed check, for example, 'file is a directory'

errors.name: NotExistent
errors.comment: NotExistent can be used if a required object does not exist, for example, a file.

param.name: F
param.comment: F is the name of the object, for example, a filename

errors.name: AlreadyExistent
errors.comment: AlreadyExistent can be used if a required object already exists, for example, a file, but is not expected to exist.

param.name: F
param.comment: F is the name of the object, for example, a filename

errors.name: Op
errors.comment: Op can be used for failed operations on an object.

param.name: Op
param.comment: Op is the name of the failed operation, for example, 'WriteStr'

param.name: Fn
param.comment: Fn is the name of the object passed to the operation, for example, a filename

param.name: Err
param.comment: Err is the error returned by the failed operation, for example, 'file does not exist'

errors.name: NilFailed
errors.comment: NilFailed can be used if a function implementing an operation returns nil when an error was expected (e.g., in unit tests).

param.name: Op
param.comment: Op is the name of the operation, for example, 'ExistsFile'

errors.name: NilExpected
errors.comment: NilExpected can be used if a function implementing an operation returns an error when nil was expected (e.g., in unit tests).
errors.message: %v did not return nil, but nil expected

param.name: Op
param.comment: Op is the name of the operation, for example, 'ExistsFile'

errors.name: Empty
errors.comment: Empty can be used if a required object is empty but not allowed to be empty, for example, an input argument of type string.

param.name: F
param.comment: F is the name of the empty object, for example, a parameter or filename

errors.name: EqualStr
errors.comment: EqualStr can be used if a string is not equal to an expected string.
errors.message: value of %v is %v, but expected to be equal to %v

param.name: Var
param.comment: Var is the name of the variable

param.name: Actual
param.comment: Actual is the actual value of Var

param.name: Want
param.comment: Want is the expected value of Var

errors.name: TypeNotMatching
errors.comment: TypeNotMatching can be used if the type of an object does not match the expected type.

param.name: Actual
param.comment: Actual is the actual type of the object, for example, 'file'

param.name: Want
param.comment: Want is the expected or required type of the object, for example, 'directory'

errors.name: Forbidden
errors.comment: Forbidden can be used if an operation on an object is forbidden.

param.name: F
param.comment: F is the name of the forbidden object, for example, a directory or filename

errors.name: Return
errors.comment: Return can be used if an operation returns an actual value, but another return value was expected.

param.name: Op
param.comment: Op is the operation name

param.name: Actual
param.comment: Actual is the actual return value returned by Op

param.name: Want
param.comment: Want is the expected return value from Op

errors.name: Higher
errors.comment: Higher can be used if an integer fails to be at least equal to or higher than a defined lower bound.
errors.message: value of %v is %d, but expected to be at least equal to or higher than %d

param.name: Var
param.comment: Var is the name of the variable

param.name: Actual
param.comment: Actual is the actual value of Var

param.name: LowerBound
param.comment: LowerBound is the lower bound. Actual is expected to be equal to or higher than LowerBound

errors.name: EqualInt
errors.comment: EqualInt can be used if an integer fails to be equal to an expected value.
errors.message: value of %v is %d, but expected to be equal to %d

param.name: Var
param.comment: Var is the name of the variable

param.name: Actual
param.comment: Actual is the actual value of Var

param.name: Want
param.comment: Want is the expected value of Var

errors.name: Equal
errors.comment: Equal can be used if two variables are not equal when they are expected to be equal.
errors.message: variable %v does not equal variable %v, but is expected to be equal

param.name: X
param.comment: Name of the first variable

param.name: Y
param.comment: Name of the second variable

errors.name: Lower
errors.comment: Lower can be used if an integer fails to be lower than a defined upper bound.
errors.message: value of %v is %d, but expected to be lower than %d

param.name: Var
param.comment: Var is the name of the variable

param.name: Actual
param.comment: Actual is the actual value of Var

param.name: HigherBound
param.comment: HigherBound is the upper bound. Actual is expected to be lower than HigherBound

errors.name: NotSet
errors.comment: NotSet can be used if a required object or configuration is not set, for example, an environment variable.

param.name: F
param.comment: F is the name of the unset object, for example, an environment variable name

errors.name: NotAvailable
errors.comment: NotAvailable can be used if a service is not available.

param.name: S
param.comment: S is the name of the unavailable service

param.name: Err
param.comment: Err is the underlying error returned by the service

errors.name: Equalf
errors.comment: Equalf can be used if a float value is not equal to an expected value.
errors.message: value of %v is %f, but expected to be equal to %f

param.name: Var
param.comment: Var is the name of the variable

param.name: Actual
param.comment: Actual is the actual value of Var

param.name: Want
param.comment: Want is the expected value of Var

errors.name: NonPrintable
errors.comment: NonPrintable can be used if a string contains non-printable runes when only printable runes are permitted.
errors.message: %v contains non-printable runes, but only printable runes are allowed

param.name: F
param.comment: F is the name of the string that should only contain printable runes

errors.name: NotEqual
errors.comment: NotEqual can be used if two variables are equal when they are not permitted to be equal.
errors.message: variable %v equals variable %v, but not allowed to equal

param.name: X
param.comment: Name of the first variable

param.name: Y
param.comment: Name of the second variable

errors.name: Duplicate
errors.comment: Duplicate can be used if an object already exists but must be unique, for example, a key or identifier.
errors.message: %v is a duplicate and already exists

param.name: F
param.comment: F is the name of the duplicate object, for example, a key name

errors.name: Locked
errors.comment: Locked can be used if a resource or service is locked, for example, because an operation is still in progress.

param.name: S
param.comment: S is the name of the locked service or resource

errors.name: MethodNotAllowed
errors.comment: MethodNotAllowed can be used if an operation or HTTP method is not allowed on a given resource.

param.name: Method
param.comment: Method is the name of the disallowed method

param.name: Resource
param.comment: Resource is the name of the target resource

errors.name: InvalidJson
errors.comment: InvalidJson can be used if a JSON payload is invalid and cannot be parsed.

param.name: Err
param.comment: Err is the error that occurred while parsing the JSON

errors.name: InvalidFormat
errors.comment: InvalidFormat can be used if a string is invalid and cannot be parsed according to the expected format.

param.name: S
param.comment: S is the string that has an invalid format

errors.name: InvalidTimestampFormat
errors.comment: InvalidTimestampFormat can be used if a timestamp string cannot be parsed.

param.name: Err
param.comment: Err is the error that occurred while parsing the timestamp

errors.name: StatusNotMatching
errors.comment: StatusNotMatching can be used if an actual status does not match the expected status.
errors.message: status does not match: expected %d, actual %d

param.name: Expected
param.comment: Expected is the expected status

param.name: Actual
param.comment: Actual is the actual status received

errors.name: NotFound
errors.comment: NotFound can be used if a required object cannot be found, for example, a file or a database record.

param.name: F
param.comment: F is the name of the missing object, for example, a filename or key

errors.name: UnexpectedField
errors.comment: UnexpectedField can be used if an unexpected field is encountered in parsed input.

param.name: F
param.comment: F is the name of the unexpected field

errors.name: UnexpectedError
errors.comment: UnexpectedError can be used if a received error does not match the expected error (e.g., in unit tests).

param.name: Expected
param.comment: Expected is the expected error

param.name: Actual
param.comment: Actual is the received error

errors.name: NoChanges
errors.comment: NoChanges can be used if no changes are found (for example, no staged Git changes).

param.name: F
param.comment: F is the name of the object without changes
